sets.title: Invoice totalling in foreach vs functional idiom
sets.description: The same invoice line-item totalling computation (subtotal, tax, grand total) written in two genuinely different idioms: carrier A uses an explicit foreach accumulation loop; carrier B uses array_reduce — a functional-style accumulation. Both are behaviorally verified equivalent via invoice_totals equivalence_test.php. These idioms share almost no token sequences, so token/line tools cannot pair them; AST-canonicalizing tools face the same barrier since the control-flow structures differ fundamentally. Only semantic-class detectors (embedding/LLM) are expected to detect this clone pair. NOTE: seed invoice_totals has only one API-01 variant (array_reduce), so this set has 2 carriers (foreach + array_reduce) rather than the ideal 3.
sets.notes: The two carriers compute identical results for all inputs (verified by equivalence_test.php). Carrier A uses traditional foreach-loop accumulation; carrier B uses array_reduce with an anonymous function accumulator — both compute subtotal, discount, tax, shipping, total, and item count. The benchmark showed jscpd (token-based) finds this pair with recall 1.0 because they share many normalized tokens (variable names, operators, literals). AST-based and semantic detectors can also detect it. Token-based detection is TRUE for this set (not false as typical L7) because the foreach and array_reduce idioms share sufficient lexical similarity. SEED LIMITATION: invoice_totals has only one API-01 variant, so this set has 2 carriers (foreach + array_reduce) instead of the ideal 3 with three distinct idioms.

distractors.reason: near-miss: same invoice-domain vocabulary (lineItems, qty, unitPrice) and similar foreach-over-items shape, but computes revenue/cost/margin summary — a different result with different arithmetic (costRate multiplication, margin ratio), not a duplicate of computeTotals
